text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Franjo Tudjman to open a new section of motorway in northern Croatia, linking Hungarian border crossing at Gorican and Croatian town of Cakovec, on Wednesday.
- A van carrying Zdravko Tomac, presidential candidate from the Socal Democratic party, was stoned near Zadar.
- Croatian branch of Helsinki Watch Committee reports conditions in Knin, former rebel Serb stronghold, improving and 2,800 Serbs have returned since 1995.
- Croatian fishermen caught only 6,000 tons of fish in 1996, 10 percent of the pre-war quantity.
- In relation to German mark, Croatian currency kuna was 3.9 percent stronger in May than three years ago.
- Deutsche Bank, sixth largest bank in the world, opened a branch in Zagreb, but still has no private business.
- Editorial says Croatian army is now "worthy of NATO" and has matured into a highly professionalised force that will knock on the door of the Partnership for Peace military cooperation programme.
- Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa, accompanied by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, opened a bridge at Brcko, linking eastern Croatia and northeastern Bosnia.
- Registration begins today for all those eligible for free shares under government voucher privatisation scheme. Over 400,000 people expected to register by October.

- Jovan Bamburac, one of the five Serb representatives in parliament, says he does not expect the reintegration of the last Serb enclave Eastern Slavonia to go smoothly, especially when it comes to the key issue - the return of all refugees.
- A piece of stone tile, engraved with an inscription in the old Croatian alphabet, was found in southern Croatia and dates from between the 10th and 12th century.
- Croatian Government Office for Refugees reminds all Bosnian citizens in Croatia the registration for Bosnian municipal election ends on June 7.

- The Social Democrats, whose candidate will challenge president Franjo Tudjman in election on June 15, protest to state election commission over state television which lavishly promotes Tudjman, even in entertainment programmes.
